title: The Flow of Thought
coreMove: Give thinking a playable structure: a real question, symbolic rules, visible progress, and a next move that keeps curiosity active.
sourcePressure: Thought becomes flow when symbols, rules, language, history, science, philosophy, amateur inquiry, and lifelong learning give the mind structured challenge.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turn intellectual flow into study tips, credential worship, or vague curiosity praise.

sourceAnchors.name: Clio
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen heading index includes Befriending Clio, invoking the muse of history as a way into historical inquiry
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: To befriend Clio is to treat history less like a shelf of dates and more like a living puzzle about why people chose as they did.

sourceAnchors.name: the rules of the games of the mind
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen heading index frames thought as games of the mind with rules
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A mind gets absorbed when the thinking has rules, the way a game does: moves matter because not every move is allowed.

hook: generic the flow of thought definition opener
open with a named person staring at a phone and realizing the abstract lesson
start with comfort versus challenge in slogan form
counterintuition: Most people assume X, but actually Y
The real problem is not X, it is Y
You do not need more discipline, you need better systems
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on your life
Write down three things you learned
Notice your attention without changing the situation
examples: timestamp plus protagonist plus laptop plus decision in every case
generic office, classroom, kitchen, commute rotation
same visible beat with different props

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a library volunteer turning local history into an inquiry puzzle
exampleSpecs.audience: retirees and volunteers who want mental challenge without formal schooling
exampleSpecs.stakes: the archive project will stay dull unless he finds a question inside it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the archive room smells of paper, and Thomas chooses one unanswered migration pattern instead of alphabetizing another box
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The archive room fan clicks above three banker boxes

exampleSpecs.domain: a crossword constructor learning rule-bound wordplay
exampleSpecs.audience: language lovers who consume puzzles but want deeper involvement
exampleSpecs.stakes: her first grid either becomes random cleverness or a game with constraints
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she erases a corner, writes the theme rule at the top, and tests each clue against that rule before filling squares
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Eraser crumbs collect in the corner of the grid

exampleSpecs.domain: a lab technician keeping science alive after routine work
exampleSpecs.audience: technical workers whose job has become automatic
exampleSpecs.stakes: comfort could freeze his learning just when equipment changes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts the calibration will stay boring unless he asks why the drift appears, then runs one side test for feedback
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 3:42 p.m., Andrew watches the calibration line drift

exampleSpecs.domain: a philosophy reading group host avoiding abstract display
exampleSpecs.stakes: the group will collapse if it becomes status performance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a member asks what the passage means, and Anke turns it into a lived question each person can answer from one decision that week
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Are we supposed to understand this sentence?" someone asks

exampleSpecs.domain: a software tester using a bug as a mental game
exampleSpecs.audience: professionals who need fresh challenge inside familiar work
exampleSpecs.stakes: a stubborn defect blocks release and his usual checklist has failed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you reconstruct the bug by writing the rule each failed theory broke, then find the one condition the logs keep hiding
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You have run the same failing test eleven times

exampleSpecs.domain: an adult learner building a map of bird calls
exampleSpecs.audience: lifelong learners who need feedback outside school
exampleSpecs.stakes: without structure her new interest will become another abandoned app
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast passive listening walks with the morning she records three calls, checks them against a guide, and marks one improvement
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Aanya thought she liked birds until the calls all blurred together

skillTargets: distinguishing amateur depth from credential seeking
using words, history, science, or philosophy as flow domains

tryThisNowSpec: Turn one vague curiosity into a playable question, then write the rule for what counts as progress in the next ten minutes.
